# 2 Samuel Chapter 7 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 174r–175v | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/2SA_007_page_001.jpg, 2SA_007_page_002.jpg, 2SA_007_page_003.jpg | **DSS:** 4QSamᵃ (4Q51) fragments extant — significant for Davidic covenant

---

**7:1** And-it-was when sat the-king in-his-house, and-YHWH had-given-rest to-him from-around, from-all his-enemies,

**7:2** and-said the-king to-Natan the-prophet, "See, please, I [am]-dwelling in-a-house of-cedar [erez], and-[the]-ark of-the-God [is]-dwelling in-[the]-midst of-the-curtain [yeri'ah]."

**7:3** And-said Natan to the-king, "All that [is] in-your-heart, go, do, for YHWH [is] with-you."

**7:4** And-it-was in-that night, and-was [the]-word of-YHWH to Natan, saying,

**7:5** "Go and-say to my-servant, to-David: 'Thus says YHWH: Shall-you build for-Me a-house for-My-dwelling?

**7:6** For not I-have-dwelt in-a-house from-the-day I-brought-up [the]-sons of-Yisra'el from-Mitsrayim and-unto this day, and-I-have-been walking-about [mithalekh] in-a-tent and-in-a-tabernacle [mishkan].

**7:7** In-all [places]-where I-walked-about among-all [the]-sons of-Yisra'el, did-I-speak a-word with one of-[the]-tribes [shivtey] of-Yisra'el, whom I-commanded to-shepherd my-people Yisra'el, saying: Why have-you-not built for-Me a-house of-cedars?'

**7:8** And-now, thus you-shall-say to-my-servant, to-David: 'Thus says YHWH of-hosts: I took-you from the-pasture [naveh], from-after the-flock, to-be ruler [nagid] over my-people, over Yisra'el.

**7:9** And-I-was with-you in-all where you-went, and-I-cut-off all your-enemies from-before-you, and-I-made for-you a-name great as-[the]-name of-the-great-ones who [are] in-the-earth.

**7:10** And-I-will-appoint a-place for-my-people, for-Yisra'el, and-I-will-plant-them and-they-will-dwell under-it [i.e., in their own place], and-not they-will-tremble again; and-not will-add sons of-wickedness [bney-avlah] to-afflict-them as-before,

**7:11** and-from the-day I-commanded judges over my-people Yisra'el. And-I-will-give-rest to-you from-all your-enemies. And-declares to-you YHWH that a-house [bayit] YHWH will-make for-you.

**7:12** When your-days are-fulfilled and-you-lie with your-fathers, I-will-raise-up your-seed [zera'] after-you, who will-come-out from-your-bowels [me'eykha], and-I-will-establish his-kingdom.

**7:13** He shall-build a-house for-My-name, and-I-will-establish [the]-throne of-his-kingdom forever [ad olam].

**7:14** I will-be to-him as-a-father, and-he will-be to-Me as-a-son. When he-does-wrong [ba-ha'avotō], I-will-discipline-him with-[the]-rod of-men and-with-[the]-stripes of-[the]-sons of-adam.

**7:15** And-My-covenant-faithfulness [chasdi] shall-not depart from-him, as I-removed [it] from-with Sha'ul, whom I-removed from-before-you.

**7:16** And-shall-be-established [ne'eman] your-house and-your-kingdom forever before-you [lefaneykha]; your-throne shall-be established forever [ad olam].'

**7:17** According-to-all these words and-according-to-all this vision, so spoke Natan to David.

**7:18** And-came the-king David and-sat before YHWH and-said, "Who [am]-I, my-Lord YHWH, and-what [is] my-house, that You-have-brought-me unto here?

**7:19** And-this-was-still small in-Your-eyes, my-Lord YHWH, and-You-spoke also concerning-[the]-house of-Your-servant for-a-distant-[time] [le-merachoq]. And-this [is the]-instruction [torah] of-the-adam [ha-adam], my-Lord YHWH.

**7:20** And-what can-David add again to-speak to-You? And-You know Your-servant, my-Lord YHWH.

**7:21** For-[the]-sake of-Your-word and-according-to Your-heart You-have-done all this greatness, to-make-known [to] Your-servant.

**7:22** Therefore You-are-great, my-Lord YHWH, for there-is-none like-You, and-there-is-no God besides-You, according-to-all that we-have-heard with-our-ears.

**7:23** And-who [is]-like Your-people, like-Yisra'el, one [goy echad] nation in-the-earth, whom God went to-redeem for-Himself as-a-people, and-to-make for-Himself a-name, and-to-do for-you [plural] the-great-[thing] and-fearful-[things] for-Your-land, before Your-people whom You-redeemed for-Yourself from-Mitsrayim, [from] nations and-their-gods?

**7:24** And-You-established for-Yourself Your-people Yisra'el as-a-people for-You forever, and-You, YHWH, became for-them as-God.

**7:25** And-now, YHWH God, the-word that You-spoke concerning Your-servant and-concerning his-house, establish [it] forever, and-do as You-have-spoken.

**7:26** And-may-be-great Your-name forever, saying, 'YHWH of-hosts [is] God over Yisra'el'; and-[the]-house of-Your-servant David shall-be established before-You.

**7:27** For You, YHWH of-hosts, God of-Yisra'el, You-have-uncovered [the]-ear of-Your-servant, saying, 'A-house I-will-build for-you.' Therefore Your-servant has-found [his]-heart to-pray to-You this prayer.

**7:28** And-now, my-Lord YHWH, You [are] the-God, and-Your-words are [ha-emet] truth, and-You-spoke to Your-servant this-good.

**7:29** And-now, be-willing and-bless [the]-house of-Your-servant to-be forever before-You, for You, my-Lord YHWH, have-spoken, and-from-Your-blessing may-[the]-house of-Your-servant be-blessed forever."

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.7 — shivtey vs. shoftey:** The MT reads שִׁבְטֵי (tribes), but the parallel passage in 1 Chr 17:6 and the LXX read "judges" (שֹׁפְטֵי). The 4QSamᵃ fragment may support "judges." Both make contextual sense; I follow the MT.

**v.11 — bayit wordplay:** The pivot of the entire chapter is the wordplay on *bayit* (house): David wants to build YHWH a *bayit* (temple); YHWH will build David a *bayit* (dynasty). This reversal is the theological heart of the Davidic covenant.

**v.14 — ba-ha'avotō:** Literally "in his doing wrong/iniquity." YHWH promises to discipline — not abandon — David's offspring. This clause distinguishes the unconditional Davidic covenant from the conditional Mosaic covenant.

**v.16 — ne'eman...ad olam:** The throne is described as *ne'eman* (established/faithful/trustworthy) — from the root א-מ-נ, the same root as *emet* (truth) and *amen*.

**v.19 — torah ha-adam:** One of the most debated phrases in Samuel. Literally "this is the instruction/law of the man/humanity." Interpretations range from "this is the charter for humanity" to "this is how you deal with a mere human" to "this is a revelation concerning humanity's future."

**4QSamᵃ note:** The DSS fragments (4Q51) preserve variants of this chapter that are significant for the Davidic covenant theology. The LXX (Vaticanus) also diverges in several places, especially v.7 and v.16.

*— EMET*
